verses.5: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
verses.6: The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.
verses.7: The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
verses.8: The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
verses.9: The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.
verses.10: Cush fathered Nimrod, the one who began to be mighty in the land.
verses.11: Egypt fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphthuhim,
verses.12: Pathrusim, Casluhim (from whom the Philistines emerged), and Caphtorim.
verses.13: Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth.
verses.14: He also fathered the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.
verses.15: The Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
verses.16: The Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
verses.17: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. Also, Utz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
verses.18: Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
verses.19: To Eber were born two sons: the name of the one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother was Joktan.
verses.20: Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
verses.21: He also fathered Hadarom, Uzal, and Diklah.
verses.23: Ofir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
verses.28: The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishmael.
verses.29: These are their descendants: Ishmael's firstborn was Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mishma.
verses.31: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.
verses.32: The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine, were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan were Sheba and Dedan.
verses.33: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldadah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
verses.34: Abraham fathered Isaac. The sons of Isaac were Esau and Israel.
verses.35: The sons of Esau were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korach.
verses.36: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
verses.37: The sons of Reuel were Nahath, Zerah, Shamma, and Mizzah.
verses.38: The sons of Seir were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan.
verses.39: The sons of Lotan were Horim and Homan. His sister was Timna.
verses.40: The sons of Shobal were Alvan, Manachath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah.
verses.41: The sons of Anah were Dishon. The sons of Dishon were Hamran, Eshban, Itheran, and Keran.
verses.42: The sons of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishon were Uz and Aran.
verses.43: These were the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before any king ruled the children of Israel: Bela, son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
verses.44: Bela died, and Jobab, son of Zerah from Bozrah, ruled in his place.
verses.45: Jobab died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanites, ruled in his place.
verses.46: Husham died, and Hadad, son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the field of Moab, ruled in his place. The name of his city was Avith.
verses.47: Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah ruled in his place.
verses.48: Samlah died, and Saul from the land of the River ruled in his place.
verses.49: Saul died, and Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, ruled in his place.
verses.50: Baal-Hanan died, and Hadad ruled in his place. The name of his city was Paei, and the name of his wife was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezah.
verses.51: Hadad died, and these were the chieftains of Edom: Chieftain Teman, Chieftain Alvah, Chieftain Jetheth,
verses.52: Chieftain Oholibamah, Chieftain Elah, Chieftain Pinon,
verses.53: Chieftain Kenaz, Chieftain Teman, Chieftain Mibzar,
verses.54: Chieftain Magdiel, Chieftain Iram. These were the chieftains of Edom.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 34: The Hebrew text lists Israel as the second son of Isaac, aligning with the narrative of Jacob being renamed Israel, though the text here may reflect a later editorial addition.  
- v. 50: "Mehetabel" is preserved in the name table as a proper name, with the phrase "daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezah" preserving the Hebrew genealogical structure.  
- v. 51–54: The listing of chieftains follows the structure of the Hebrew text, which includes multiple chieftainships but does not specify their relationships or reigns.
